title.value: Supervised Seeded Iterated Learning for Interactive Language Learning
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the top of the paper, including the authors and affiliations.
title.quote: Supervised Seeded Iterated Learning for Interactive Language Learning

analysis.description: The paper addresses the issue of language drift in training language models through interaction. It discusses two methods, Supervised Selfplay (S2P) and Seeded Iterated Learning (SIL), to counter language drift. The authors introduce a new method, Supervised Seeded Iterated Learning (SSIL), which combines the strengths of both S2P and SIL to minimize language drift and improve task performance in conversational agents. The effectiveness of SSIL is demonstrated through experiments in a translation game setting.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments and empirical evaluation of the proposed SSIL method, as well as comparisons with existing methods (S2P and SIL) through metrics such as BLEU scores and negative log-likelihood.
type.quote: We report the task and grounding scores of vanilla Gumbel, S2P, SIL, and SSIL in Figure 2.

name.justification: The paper discusses conversational agents and language drift, which are key topics in Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Language drift has been one of the major ob- stacles to train language models through in- teraction.

name.justification: The focus on conversational agents interacting through language to solve tasks highlights this subfield.
name.quote: In this goal-oriented dialogue setting, the conversational agents are often designed to compose with predefined language utterances.

name.justification: The experimental setting includes a translation game which is directly related to machine translation tasks.
name.quote: We replicate the translation game setting from (Lee et al., 2019) as it was designed to study language drift.

name.justification: The SSIL model is proposed as a new algorithm combining aspects of SIL and S2P to address language drift.
name.quote: We propose to combine SIL with S2P by ap- plying an S2P loss in the interactive stage of SIL. We show that the resulting Supervised Seeded It- erated Learning (SSIL) algorithm manages to get the best of both algorithms in the translation game.

is_contributed.justification: The SSIL model is introduced for the first time in this paper as a contribution to improving language learning in AI.
